# Handoff log

Newest entry on top. Every phase session ends by adding an entry here and tagging the commit `phase-NN-done`.

### Fluid track FL-1a - pacer and ladder bugs (no look change) - 2026-10-30
Branch `track/fluid` (round 1 lane, beside FL-1b and FL-2a; FL-1b's commits merged in). Plan approved by the owner's
standing answer (fluid-track.md section 1). Code: the frame scheduler's pacing, the automatic quality's feed; no
look change. No tag (the track's tag comes at FL-7).
- Facts checked against the code (73b2f8b1 + FL-1b): all of section 5's items 3-5 hold. Two more found: the walk
  view never fed the fps overlay (`walkView.opt.meter` is never set), so the overlay counted its own `meter` task's
  ticks at the set rate, not the world's frames, and that task never stopped; the old refresh estimate needed a
  tick with under 3 ms of work, so a page drawing every tick never read its screen. Simulated, the old pacer at 120 Hz
  and cap 60 gives 16.7 / 25 / 8.3 after one miss.
- Changed:
  - game/js/logic/frame-pace.js (new, pure, in both pages and the Studio's logic worker): `refreshTick` /
    `refreshPeriod` (the period from every tick: a delta counts when the tick before had under half of it as work or
    when it is quicker than the period so far; the lower quarter of the last 0.5 s, near ones averaged, every 0.1 s,
    no list), `paceSlot` (a rate as whole refreshes, nearest; the half rate doubles it), `paceDue` (locked to the
    beat: `next = max(next + T, ts + T - V/2)`, due from `next`, a cap change starts the beat at once; each task's
    `shown` interval in refreshes, `missed` (over a slot plus half a refresh), `misses`, `frames`), `ladderFeed` /
    `ladderTake` (the automatic quality's feed), `phoneAgent` (one phone test: Android, iPhone, iPad, a touch Mac).
  - game/js/frame-scheduler.js: uses them; `frameScheduler.period` (ms) beside `hz` (now whole, from the period);
    `frameScheduler.half` and `frameHalf(on)` for FL-3a's controller (the tasks whose cap is the set rate take it);
    the GPU counters wrap only a tick with a task due, and `frameScheduler.counted` marks it; a task is dropped on
    its third throw in a row; the scheduler meters the main task itself (dio, else scene, else map: fps from its runs,
    ms from its time); `frameCount` is kept for its callers and does nothing.
  - game/js/engine/gpu-counters.js: after a counted tick that drew nothing, the next count waits 250 ms.
  - game/js/walk/quality-cull.js adaptQuality: fed through `ladderTake`: below 30 a second nothing; a cap change
    resets the averages and waits 1.5 s (the menu ratchet); the counted tick left out; the target is the paced slot
    of min(cap, 60 or 999 with Balanced), so 60 on a 90 Hz screen (every second refresh) isn't read as slow. Its two
    phone tests and FRAME_WORK_MS use `phoneAgent`.
  - game/js/walk-view-gl.js: the ladder's work leaves out the one-off jobs (normal maps, program polls, ground and
    walking-grid preparation, ensureGround and the map-cache swap, grass, far props, the near ring); `walkView.slow`
    skips the counted tick. The histogram and the full frame time are unchanged.
  - game/js/debug-menu.js: the overlay adds no task; it says "(half rate)" when the half rate is on.
- Not done, for other lanes (their files): the other phone tests still disagree: walk/walk-state.js PREP_BUDGET_MS,
  walk/lighting.js PHONE_LAMPS, battle-3d.js PHONE_BATTLE, walk-view-gl.js PHONE, engine/webgl.js:1555,
  person-art.js, walk-view.js GROUND_CACHE_SIZE (all can call `phoneAgent(navigator.userAgent,
  navigator.maxTouchPoints)`). battle-stage.js's ladder (FL-3a) still aims at `min(userFps(), hz)`: on a 90 Hz
  screen it reads 45 as slow; it should aim at `paceSlot(...) * frameScheduler.period`. FL-1b's
  `debugLog.slotMs` uses min(fps, hz) too: on 90 Hz every 22.2 ms frame sits on its line; the scheduler's
  `tasks.get('dio').missed`/`.shown` are the paced numbers (TD-4).
- Risky: an iPad (it reports a Mac) is now a phone in the automatic quality (graphics waits read as main-thread
  work, the resolution not below 0.6) and gets the phone's 8 ms one-off budget. The refresh can read low if the GPU
  holds back every frame with light main-thread work (a GPU-bound phone): then the slot follows what the page gets.
  The battle's quality now reads the dio task's frames in a 3D battle (before: the scene task's). Frame times only
  on the phone.
- Verified: the gates (tools/test/frame-pace.test.mjs, 13 tests, Node vsync simulation with the real qualityStep):
  120 Hz cap 60 one miss → 16.7 / 25 / 16.7, no 8.3; 61 Hz → 0 drops in 10 s; 120 → 60 re-read within 1 s; every
  frame 40 ms → a steady 50 ms; 8 window/screen cycles at 11 ms → q and R unchanged (phone and desktop); 90 Hz at
  5 ms → no step in 60 s; plus a slow frame still steps. gpu-counters test for the back-off. Lint, types, format,
  modules, data, build clean; unit tests 2405 of 2406 with smoke running beside them (the 1,000-maps timing test,
  which passes alone); smoke 7 of 7 (350 s) before and after merging FL-1b; QUICK_RESULT.
- Ask me before (not settled by section 1): **a setting between divisors** (60 on a 90 Hz screen: 45 or 90). Today
  it stays 45 (the nearest whole slot, as before) and the ladder aims at 45 there. Recommendation as in section 7:
  the higher one while the controller holds it, else the lower, decided in FL-3a.
- Next: round 2 (FL-2b, FL-3a, FL-6) once FL-1b and FL-2a are done; FL-3a uses `frameHalf` and `paceSlot`.
- For the owner on the phone: the fps overlay now counts the world's own frames; open and close Team a few times
  and check Q and the resolution stay put in the debug log.

### Fluid track FL-0 - the plan: hold the frame rate you set, batching, render layering, a fluid UI - 2026-10-29
Branch `ccr-36d73c36-2xv56p` (the cloud session's own, at main 73b2f8b1). Plan approved in Plan Mode with the owner's
answers. Docs only: the plan, web research and read-only code studies (nine studies, seven verifiers that tried to
refute the key claims, a plan critic); no code changed.
- Changed: docs/phases/fluid-track.md (new: the owner's answers, the numbers, "are assets batched correctly?" as a
  table, render layering from the research against this game's frame, why the set fps isn't held, sessions
  FL-0b..FL-7 with gates, Ask me before, sources); ROADMAP's "Fluid track" row (top of "Tracks alongside") and a
  pointer on phase 20's row; BRANCHES rows for `track/fluid` and this branch.
- The owner's answers: a steady half rate when the set rate can't be held; on phones automatic quality may thin far
  props and folk, use a 2048 far shadow map, tint the HUD glass while walking and draw far trees as one picture;
  Pictures in batches and Sky last on by default (after three small fixes); the world frozen behind menus and windows.
- Found, not changed (all in the track file with file:line):
  - Batching: pictures are not batched by default (`quality.spriteInstances` off): one draw and about 30 GL calls
    each; leaf clumps are 260 separate textures; each fountain is 151-247 draws; spin layers 96 where 7 would do; the
    ground (316k triangles) is never culled and drawn in up to 5 passes. Models, shadow pictures, grass, rain:
    batched.
  - Every depth-writing scene shader contains `discard`, so the Adreno's LRZ never gets a write; the sky is drawn
    first; cut-outs come before the opaque models.
  - Chrome and Opera on Android give a page every other refresh above about 108 Hz (120 → 60): the 120 option gives
    60 there. iOS about 60, 30 in Low Power Mode. Firefox adds no cap.
  - Automatic quality aims at 60 at most (not the setting) except on Balanced, counts background jobs as frame cost,
    and steps down each time a menu closes (a Node simulation reaches the floor in 8 cycles).
  - The scheduler catches up after a late frame (25 then 8 ms); 60 on a 90 Hz screen runs at 45; `gl.getError` and a
    fully wrapped counted frame once a second for every player; a 4096² far shadow map plus a copy a frame on phones.
  - UI: the world draws behind menus (20 fps behind windows; a window over a screen back to 20); the theme sheet's
    12 px blur beats the phone's 9 px; the Actions button blurs behind an opaque fill; battle plates force layout
    every frame and that time lowers the battle's quality.
- Risky: nothing changed in code. Counts quoted from R2/R4 are headless and from an older commit; FL-2a re-measures.
- Verified: docs only; the key claims re-checked by the verifiers at 73b2f8b1 (corrections are in the track file).
- Next: FL-0b, the owner's phone run below; then FL-1a on `track/fluid` (the owner makes it from this branch).
- For the owner on the phone: run the Graphics cost test and the Diagnostics on the Android phone, then send the
  debug log of a Copperleaf walk by day. Note the browser and whether battery saver is on. Then make `track/fluid`
  from `ccr-36d73c36-2xv56p` and start FL-1a there.

### Fix - Kappi's stall clock counts only free walking - 2026-10-29
Branch `fix/kappi-stall-clock` from main 7f661239, PR into main. From the owner's first phone log of the new intro
(deploy 7f661239, Android, Adreno 750): New game -> the crash scene at 15.6 s -> Cartotter picked at 42.8 s (27 s into
the scene) -> the run at 49 s -> Meadow Route -> a wild battle won; no errors. But "Kappi's cue: stall" fired 3.6 s
after the crash scene ended, and again 0.2 s after the battle: the place's stall clock (logic/kappi-tips.js) started
when the run's first look saw the place and ran on through the scene and the battle.
- Changed: `tipHold(st, free, t)` holds the clock while you aren't free to walk (kappi.js calls it every look with
  `kappiWalking()`: no scene, story, battle, sheet or room); a new place while held starts when you are free again.
- Tests: kappi-tips.test.mjs, one more (the log's two cases and a place reached while held); 16 of 16. check-fast
  "Kappi's tips" passes; lint, types, format.
- Also in the log, not fixed here: the run's walk at 23-31 fps with quality stepped down to q4 and resolution 0.6
  within 29 s (planting the grass and drawing sprites lead the slow frames, on the route more than on the landing);
  the graphics estimate 307 MB, the landing's peak 322 MB (TD's phone budget is 300). For the load and test tracks.

### Load track - the crossing hitch: the day's water remade in the background, the walking grid built ahead - 2026-10-28
Branch `claude/new-session-bcxme1` (from main 485674b5; main merged in at a3bc2421, 76aea599 (#306 with it), 4423a457 and ed5c6857). Plan approved in Plan Mode. The owner: "there's still a hiccup
when moving from a route to another route", with their PC debug log (10:36, RTX 2070, DPR 2.5) and diagnostics report
(10:30). No look changes, except when the water appears (below).
- **Found** (the log, then the code):
  - The full test's crossing into Thicket Route: one frame of 3238 ms ("building the ground mesh"); the second time a
    926 ms frame, a 4.7 s hold (`crossings.heldMaxMs` 4665) at about 22 fps, then 392 ms at the switch. Both logged
    "water by the weather" as the day turned.
  - run-world.js `runWaterWeatherSync`: when the day's weather changed *any* run place's water, it cleared every view,
    put a remade one on screen and set `walkRenderer.hkey = ''`, so the next frame's `swapMapCache('', hk)` could not
    use the cache and built the visible ground in one go. The next view, prepared ahead, was thrown away too.
  - `navGrid` built every new view's walking grid in one frame (14 slow frames in the log, 75-90 ms, worst 595 ms on
    the PC). load-track.md said "on a seam it is prepared ahead"; it wasn't (corrected there).
- **Changed:**
  - seamless-world.js: `seamlessDropViewsOf` drops only the views that show a changed place (`seamlessViewUses`, now
    also used by map-files.js); no `gen++` (the seams' memo holds heights, not water). The view on screen keeps drawing;
    `seamlessRemakeTick` (from `seamlessPrepareAhead`) gets its new version ready and swaps it in (swapMapCache finds
    it). `seamlessGate` crosses into a ready earlier version (`seamlessWorld.was`) rather than wait; `shiftWalkView`
    takes it and remakes it after. Stats: `remade`, `remadeMs`, `early` (the debug log's `world.crossings`).
  - walk-view.js: `navGridSteps` (the grid a row or 32 props a step; `navGrid` runs it in one go, the same arrays);
    `navPrepare` / `navPrepWork` build up to three grids ahead in the frame budget (walk-view-gl.js, next to
    `groundPrepWork`); `navReady` is part of `seamlessViewReady`. `walkView.navBuilding` holds the view being built
    (heights.js, `mapBridges`), not `true`. `walkView.navBuilds` counts grids built in one go.
  - heights.js: the steep pass as steps too; `navGrid`'s wrapper takes a kept or ahead grid without looking at the
    heights again.
  - tools/check-fast.py: "A seam on a day the weather changes the water in view" (its own run page). Fails on main
    (the ground built in one go, 2.9 s headless, and the walking grid); passes after, and checks the grid built ahead
    equals one built in one go. The plan's Node unit test for that became this in-browser comparison (walk-view.js
    needs the page).
- **Found, not changed** (the same log, for their owners):
  - The full test failed "A room that opens in place" (the town's walking grid changed by 236 cells after the room)
    and "Light lab" (one draw call refused, GL error 1282, also logged at "Fog in the air: dawn fog").
  - Copperleaf's opening hitch, "setting up the ground" 3.5 s on the PC: the same `buildGroundMesh`, on a place
    opening (behind its fade). Next for this track.
  - The diagnostics report's `passed: false` doesn't say which step failed (self-test.js `diagnosticsSummary` keeps
    only the walk, battle, world map and memory steps), and tools/read-debug-log.py can't read a diagnostics report.
  - tools/check-load.py `--only=moves --site=game` didn't get ready in 300 s here (the unbundled source).

    ready (seconds on a phone, headless 9 s), at once, instead of in a freeze.
  - A crossing now also waits for the next view's walking grid (built ahead in the frame's budget). Walking straight
    at a seam fast could hold a little longer; at the view's edge it is built on the spot, as before.
  - Not measured on a phone. Headless only ranks the causes.

Plan approved in Plan Mode. One cause per commit. No test skipped or loosened; one dead step removed (below).
- Found (CI logs of main's 5 push runs to 07c9b284, then reproduced here with the real check):
  - **The two Studio checks (5/5, real):** the world map look's last step opened the Route stops tab and its landmark
    picker, both removed in SA-3. The unknown tab fell back to Wild encounters, which drew every Billie; the check's
    data helper set `studioState.rigs={}`, so each one 404'd at `art/billionaires/<id>.png` (2077 here). The loads
    still failing spilled into the Camera section's error window (alone it had 0 errors).
  - **The Studio's Model mode, `reading 'banter'` (1/5, real):** HB-10d's `squareChat` read `gameData.banter` and
    called `squareMood`/`squareTalk`, none loaded on the Studio page; a square folk speaking in a Studio preview threw
    in the draw loop. Reproduced by forcing it.
  - **Timing on the CI runner** (wall-clock limits on what moves by frames; the game clock moves at most 60 ms a frame):
    the run's seam (4/5: the next view is held until built, about 140 frames, 61 s at ~2 fps, limit 60 s); the bowl's
    zoom out (2/5, 10 s); the orbit's hold-right (2/5: 67 frames measured, 60 s); Tall ground's `drawing()` (1/5: 3
    frames in 40 s, beside the Studio's 404 storm) and, seen on this PR's runs, its silhouette (20 s) and `stand()` (30
    frames in 60 s; a runner at under 0.5 fps).
  - **The pasture (2/5, the test's clock):** its Billies walk to the town square on a schedule by the page's clock
    (HB-10c), which starts at 12:30 on every check page: one leaves 73 s in. A slow run reached the last step after
    that and saw two leave, not one. Reproduced by waiting past 80 s.
  - **The job's 30-minute limit (this PR's push run):** the Studio's page (about 6 min of checks one after another)
    ran last, alone.
  - **Behind things (2/5), not reproduced** (3 of 3 passed): 85 frames drew and you were still "hidden", so not
    slowness. Measured: the buddy stays within a metre of you, sometimes just between the camera and you.
- Changed (tools/check-fast.py unless said): the dead landmark step removed; the Studio data helper keeps the piece
  sheets (`RIGS_NEXT`, as studio-app.js); `squareChat` returns no lines without the game data or the square's logic
  (game/js/walk-view.js); the seam wait calls `groundPrepWork(50)` (as check-quick.py's `cross(prep_ms)`);
  `until_drawn` (seconds and frames, capped) for the bowl (10 s + 10 map frames) and Tall ground's silhouette (20 s +
  60 frames); the orbit walk 60 s + up to 300 frames; the pasture check turns the square's visits off (a first commit
  that gave it frames was reverted: wrong cause); the Studio's page runs first; `drawing()` and `stand()` in tools/browser_check.py wait longer (60 s, 120 s) while the
  draw loop is alive and frames come (a dead loop or no frame still fails); Behind things turns the buddy off and its
  failure lists the buddy and the nearest folk against the camera line.
- Risky: `drawing()` and `stand()` are shared by every browser check (more lenient only when the loop is alive and frames advance).
  A seam view that never builds now fails only if 60 s of extra build time don't finish it.

  after its fix; lint, typecheck, format, check:modules, 1633 unit tests; smoke (no problems). CI on the PR (#306):

- The arithmetic (a 390×844 CSS phone, DPR 3, portrait; engine.json and Copperleaf's `cam {pitch 34, h 9, fov 1}`):
  - Scene buffer: R = min(DPR, 1.75) × `quality.resolution` 1.5 = 2.625, cut by the 1.6 MP cap to 2.205, so
    860×1861 (0.73 of the device grid), stretched to the screen with `image-rendering: auto` (walk-view-gl.js:513-524).
  - Camera at Normal: tilt 34 − 8 = 26°; height 9 × 2.1 = 18.9 m; distance 18.9 / sin 26° = 43.1 m; width at the
    aim max(11, 15 × 390/844) / 0.68 = 16.18 m (camera.js:269-306).
  - 390 / 16.18 = 24.1 CSS px a metre; a 1.75 m upright person × cos 26° (0.899) = 37.9 CSS px, 39.3 with the
    perspective (the feet nearer than the aim) = 118 device px = 86.5 buffer px.
  - Today's art is 116.4 px tall (66.5 px/m): 86.5 / 116.4 = 0.74 buffer px per art px (0.80 across). The ground (32
    px/m) is 1.66, props (34 px/m) 1.56. At 32 px/m a person is 56 px tall: 86.5 / 56 = 1.55.
  - Close (0.55): 77 CSS px, 169 buffer px: 1.45 today, 3.0 at 32 px/m. Far (1.7): 20.5 CSS px, 45 buffer px: 0.39
    today, 0.8 at 32 px/m.
  - Battle: the player's trainer (1.42 m at 2.85 m, focal 170 stage px, about 1.74 CSS px per stage px) is about 147
    CSS px = 442 device px: 3.8 device px per art px today; about 4.9 at 64 px/m.

  - Facing ignores the camera's yaw: `directionOf` (walk-view.js:3508) works in world space, and frame-items.js
    picks the view from it, so the orbit camera and turned rooms can show the wrong side.
  - The director's dark and mirrored copies lose `ax`/`ay`/`ppm` (director.js:172-199), falling back to anchor

### Air track AIR-4 - edges and shadowed haze: the light in the air by depth, blue noise, Shade in the haze - 2026-10-27
Branch `track/air` (AIR-3 merged to main as PR #251 just before; main fast-forwarded in, pushed). Plan Mode, approved;
the plan's recommendation taken: **Shade in the haze on by default** (`hazeShade` 0.5). The track is complete.
- Claims checked: the march read the full-size depth with **one nearest tap** per quarter pixel (one of 16 pixels), then
  the plain `down` blur and a bilinear stretch in grade: the cause of the fog's light halo round roofs and the player.
  **`godRays` is 0 in engine.json**, so the shafts' shade (`sa`) is off in the game: the haze shade needed its own term.
  The haze starts at about the camera distance (`fogStart = df*0.97`, ~35 m in Copperleaf) and the march stops at 48 m
  (`volMax`): the plan's "14-40 m" window caught almost nothing, so the shade covers **the haze's first 26 m** instead.
  The picture baseline is not in the repo (CI's release `baseline-0.1.0-alpha`).
- Changed (engine/post-effects.js): `vdep`, a quarter-size target with the nearest of each pixel's four corner depths,
  in metres over the far plane in two 8-bit steps (same in half-float and 8-bit targets; `VOLZ_GLSL` reads it back);
  the march reads it (back to a depth value, so the old sums hold) and starts its steps at a **64 x 64 blue-noise
  tile** (new logic/blue-noise.js, void-and-cluster, baked by tools/make-blue-noise.mjs; an R8 texture in webgl.js)
  instead of the hash; `vblur` replaces `down` for the air (the same five taps weighted by depth); grade's `volUp`
  brings it back by **nearest-depth upsampling** (bilinear where the four depths agree with the pixel's, else the
  nearest texel). Cost: one tiny pass, 5 depth reads in the blur, 4 depth + 1 air read per screen pixel in grade.
- **Shade in the haze** (`air.hazeShade` 0.5, dial "Shade in the haze" after Lamps in the fog, 0..2; 0 in PLAIN_LOOK;
  0 in battles and rooms): the march sums how much of fogit's haze (`1-exp(-1.6(t-start)/fogD)`) builds up in the
  sun's shadow over its first 26 m and darkens what is behind by 3x that x the dial, at most .35, through the existing
  alpha (no negative light: phones without float targets). No extra shadow taps; the march segment widens to the haze
  when the dial is on. The pass now also runs for the haze shade alone (shadow map needed).
- In-game full test: a new step "Fog in the air: dawn fog" (both modes; also in the diagnostics list): fog weather at
  6.6 h in the open walk scene, 3 s walking: the march (on/why), the grid, fps, the post pass's GPU ms where there
  are timers; fails on no frames or a GL error. Debug log: `fogGrid.air` {edges, hazeShade}.
- tools/look-air.py: `--air=k:v,...` (dials for every look), `--frames=N`, low-sun looks (7.6 h, 17.4 h clear).
- Tests: blue-noise.test.mjs (baked = maker, every value 16 times, almost no low frequencies, neighbours differ);
  air-edges.test.mjs (JS twins of the depth packing in 8-bit and half-float, the blur weight, the upscale's pick; the
  shader sources; the dial, default, plain look and battles); fog-grid.test.mjs's gate line updated.
- Pictures (software drawing, Copperleaf, scratchpad, sent to the owner in the session, not committed): before/after
  in dawn, morning and night fog with close-ups: **the light halo round the house roof and walls is gone**, the
  silhouette is crisp. Haze shade: at noon nearly nothing (short shadows); at low sun the haze darkens in the trees'
  and houses' shadow wedges (subtle at 0.5, ~1-3/255 on average, more in the wedges).
- Verified: lint, typecheck, format, check:modules, unit tests 1471 pass; smoke 6 of 6 in 203 s (39 shaders, 16 with
  the Frame block); the full quick check: 35 of 40 in 1799 s; the 5 steps that failed were re-run on main
  (6a482152) and on this branch: the same 3 fail on both (a train-station prop in the air, the settings tabs, the run

- Risky: **phone frame times unmeasured** (AIR-3's too): the owner's debug log after the new full-test step decides;

### Air track AIR-2 - the fog grid: a density grid round the player as an R8 3D texture, unread - 2026-10-26
Branch `track/air` (main merged in first: a conflict in AIR-1's Frame block, main's `uShFix` in the pad slot AIR-1
kept and both test blocks: resolved side by side, 2272 bytes; AIR-1's work merged before each push). Plan Mode,
approved. Nothing reads the grid yet (AIR-3), so the game's look doesn't change.
- New game/js/logic/fog-grid.js (the density as plain numbers, type-checked, in the logic worker's list) and
  game/js/walk/fog-grid.js (the texture, the uploads, the debug view), both on the game's and the Studio's pages.
  The split is mine: the plan named walk/fog-grid.js only; the logic folder is what keeps the maths testable.
- The density: each column's fog top is the mean ground on a ring about 6 m round it (8 samples), plus a layer of
  0.5-2 m (thicker in fog weather), lifted to the water level plus Mist height near water, plus a valley's mist below
  its level (`walkRenderer.valley` x the Valley mist dial), times a value noise (5 m, drifting with the wind, faster in
  storms). The amount: the scene's mist (scaled by the Low mist dial, as lighting.js does) + 0.85 x `environment.fog`.
  So a hollow fills to its rim, a hilltop's top lies below its ground (clear), none indoors (`sc.indoor` or `sc.room`).
- **Claim corrected**: the dawn mist isn't a separate input. environment.js folds it into `environment.fog` (the
  larger of the weather's fog and the morning mist), so the grid reads it once from there.
- The grid: 48 x 12 x 48 cells of 1 m, 32 x 8 x 32 on phones (`PHONE`, the user agent, as walk-view-gl.js). A ring in x
  and z: world cell (ix, iy, iz) is texel (ix mod nx, iy - oy, iz mod nz). **For AIR-3**: sample at
  `(x/(nx*cell), (y/cell - oy)/ny, z/(nz*cell))` with repeat in x and z, clamp in y (the texture's wrap modes are set
  so). The grid is in flat world positions (no `worldCurveDrop`). `fogGrid` holds `tex`, `G` (nx, ny, nz, cell, ox, oy,
  oz).
- The grid's floor follows the ground under you (4 cells below, 3 on phones). When it is 2 cells off, every row is
  refilled at once. The columns' heights are kept, and the ring's samples share heights by cell (a third of the
  reads). Uploads:
  - a step across a cell refills and uploads one slab (texSubImage3D, `UNPACK_ALIGNMENT` 1, then back to 4);
  - when the weather, mist, valley or water moves by more than 0.02, every row is refilled over a few frames (12 rows a
    frame);
  - otherwise one row every 4 frames, so the noise drifts without a seam.
- Not built indoors (the texture is freed), not updated in battles. The hook is one call after the water in
  `drawWalkFrameInner` (walk-view-gl.js), in the GPU counters' `other` pass.
- Debug: the debug menu (Tests and performance) has "Show the fog grid": the cells over 24/255 as see-through blocks,
  not saved. The debug log's report has `fogGrid`: the size, the heights read, the builds, refills, slabs and rows,
  the uploads, KB, ms per upload (the CPU's side of the call) and the fill times.
- Measured headless (software drawing, this container's CPU), Copperleaf (fixture town):
  - the first build: 48-cell grid 11.6 ms, 32-cell grid 4.7 ms (31 and 11 ms before the shared heights);
  - a slab: under 1 ms; an upload: 0.005-0.15 ms on average, at most 0.4;
  - a weather refill: about 1-2 ms a frame for 8 frames on the 48-cell grid.
  The phone's own numbers are needed: Export debug log after walking in fog.
- Tests: tools/test/fog-grid.test.mjs: a hollow fills, a hilltop stays clear (even in fog weather), none indoors (even
  with fog, mist, water and a valley), fog weather, water and a valley thicken it, the sizes, a step refills one slab
  and reads one strip of heights, and the rolled grid equals one built there.
- Verified: lint, typecheck, format, check:modules, unit tests 1320 pass. In a browser (fixture town, desktop and an
  Android user agent): the grid builds, a step uploads one slab, fog weather refills it, a room frees it, the blocks
  draw, no page errors. The smoke check passed 6 of 6, and its pictures were compared with a smoke run of AIR-1's tip
  (before AIR-2): the walk, team, guide, shop, profile, mast and run sheet match (under 1.5). phone-map and
  phone-opening-pick differ by when the picture was taken (the postcard still open; the starter card not yet up), not
  by the scene: a second run of AIR-1's tip against its first differs as much (opening-pick 77.7, battle 18.6). The exported phone debug log has `fogGrid`.
- Risky: the build happens in the frame that opens a place (about 5 ms on a phone grid here); the floor's refill on
  stairs and hills (density only, about 2 ms); the weather refill adds about 1-2 ms a frame for a few frames. 27 KB of
  texture (8 KB on phones). The Studio's walk views build it too (round `walkView.pl`).
- Next: AIR-3 (the lit march reads the grid). Tag `air-2-done` for the owner.

### HD-2D audit fixes and smart light shafts (one session, not a phase) - 2026-10-26
Branch `ccr-6f3a4696-vl6nkg` (this session's own: a cloud session pushes only there; BRANCHES.md would call it
`art/hd2d-fixes`). Started from main b87b818d (phase 20 R2-R3 merged). The owner asked for an audit of the HD-2D
effects already in the game (three code reviews and a headless on/off run of 14 effects in Copperleaf), then a fix plan
and smart, cheap god rays. **Every look change is behind its own switch, off by default** (phase 20's rule), so nothing
changes until the owner turns them on after a phone check.
- What the audit measured (headless, Copperleaf, 640x480, the share of pixels each effect changes): vignette 51%, bloom
  26%, ink 26%, outlines 20%, lamps at night 20%, shafts 13%, AO 12%, ground bumps 6%, contact shadows 6%, DOF blur 5%,
  lamp shadows 4%, ground AO 4%; **god rays 0: engine.json sets `air.godRays` 0 and `air.cheapShafts` defaults to 0, so
  the game has no light shafts at all today**.
- Smart light shafts (`air.shaftPick`, Engine > Air, off): `logic/shaft-pick.js` (pure, `tools/test/shaft-pick.test.mjs`)
  picks the cheap shafts every 0.4 s from tree crowns, the gaps between them, the two sides of houses (old 3D buildings
  and low-poly models with windows) and a place's `shafts` list; scored by shade behind the beam's foot (crowns and
  houses as circles seen toward the sun), forward scattering (looking into the light), distance from you (the walk
  camera stands 36-58 m back; the range counts from you), never over you; at most 3/5/8 by quality step and a quarter of
  the screen together; a showing shaft holds unless another scores 1.3x; fades in and out over 1.2 s. Drawn as a soft
  streaked beam (the fx program's uGlow 2). Needs `air.cheapShafts` > 0 and god rays off (as D7). Graphics test: "Sun
  gap, smart shafts".
- The fixes, each with its switch (all off): Rays follow the light (`sun.followLight`: the walk view never passed the
  light's colour, and the moon kept a full-strength warm glare); Window light faces out (`lights.windowFacing`: window
  pools were cut on a fixed +z line, wrong for every turned house; the facing rides in uLC.w); Steady shadow edges
  (`shadows.steadyEdges`: the sun maps' eye sat 2 m off the light's line, so the texel snapping drifted, test in
  tall-ground-draw.test.mjs; and the soft edge's blocker search now reaches its filter); Lamp shadows hold
  (`shadows.lampFix`: distance-scaled bias for the perspective lamp maps, a lamp's pool takes its lamp's map, lamps
  high by height above the ground); Shaded tree cores (`world.treeCoreShade`: the 30% darkening solid-props.js worked
  out and never used); Occlusion follows the slope (`shadows.aoPlane`: both ways along a line in a harmonic mean, so a
  plane gives none); Feet shade on sky light only (`shadows.groundAOSky`); Lamp light on water (`lights.onWater`);
  Outlines follow the camera (`color.inkFollow`: ink melts with the blur and fades past the focus, it faded from 25 m:
  half strength on you at zoom 1); Even bloom (`color.bloomEven`); Half-float HDR (`quality.hdrHalf`, read at start);
  Steady light on far props (`quality.normalMips`); Fronts lit as their material (`world.frontMaterial`); Building
  bumpiness (`world.buildingBumps`, 0..3, 0 = off: bricks, planks and roof tiles from the sheet's own texels, on the
  old 3D buildings and the low-poly models; the hub's houses are models now).
- Fixed without a switch (artefacts, no look intended): the near ring's bump lookup stays inside its 16 m square (seams);
  the no-worker fallback bleeds picture edges too (`bleedEdges`, shared with the helper thread).
- The light block: its float padding slot is now `uShFix` (the shadow fix bits); the size and offsets are unchanged
  (frame-block.test.mjs knows the new member).
- **Risky**: the AO slope fix went through two wrong tries (a one-pixel slope was all depth steps at 40 m; a plain mean
  misreads planes) before the harmonic mean; headless it is within noise at zoom 1, brighter close up. Building bumps at
  the usual zoom read the sheet's half size (a texel is half a screen pixel there), so they are subtle; 1.5 shows on
  roofs and planks. Lamp shadows hold and Lamp light on water showed no change in Copperleaf at night (no case near the
  player); they compile and run.
- **Found, not changed (the owner's call)**: the screen AO fades out by 36 m, nearer than you stand at zoom 1 (reaching
  further darkened every grass blade's foot); props without `ppm` are at 34 px/m (scenery.json `ppu`), people at 42 and
  66.5, Billies on a 68 grid: an art rebake to reach 32; the sprite bump's +0.18 upward tilt may be meant.
- Verified: lint, typecheck, format, check:modules, unit tests 1297 pass, the smoke check 6 of 6, `check-fast --only=town` 4 of
  5 ("A run town's shop opens (UI-5): no shop with wares" fails on main 0ba64f10 too, not this branch's), every switch on at once in Copperleaf and a
  forest trail (no errors, every lit program builds with the light block), and headless on/off pictures for each
  switch. Not judged headless (phase 20's rule): how any of it looks or costs on the phone.
- Next: the owner on the Android phone and the iPad: Graphics test (Sun gap smart shafts; Shadow court, Lamp square,
  Meadow and Depth corridor now hold the new switches) and a debug log; then one commit per switch to turn on what
  stays. After that: cavity darkening from the same sheet, short self-shadows on the ground.
### Phase 20 R3, lane context (H1-H3, H5: the resource registry, freeing, memory by kind, warm-up) - 2026-10-26
Branch `track/renderer` (one of three R3 lanes: shadows, context, battle). Plan approved ("Continue") with my
recommendations: each owner drops its own handles on a restore and makes them again lazily (no stored rebuild per
object, which would have kept every mesh's and texture's data twice); the warm-up is on by default behind its own
switch (it doesn't change the look); the other lanes may create through the registry.
- Where the phase file, R1's notes and the code differed (checked):
  - Nothing needs deleting after a loss: the old handles died with the context (a delete on them does nothing). The
    real gaps were caches fooled by the restored context being the same object, and objects dropped without delete.
  - Already fine after a restore: the sprite instance buffer (keyed on `gpuState.quad`, new with each context), the
    rain batch's arrays (kept on the program; `gpuState.P` is emptied), the models' record buffer (flushed).
  - Not fine, found here: the cloth grid (`gpuState.gridGL === gl`) kept its dead buffer after a restore.
  - No program was ever replaced within a context, but a background compile whose program had been made on the spot
    meanwhile was dropped undeleted, a failed compile left its shaders and program, and no shader was ever deleted.
  - The walk set (WALK_SHADERS, POST_EFFECT_SHADERS) compiles in one blocking go in `ensureWalkGl`; the debug log
    already blames compiles ("compiling shaders", "finishing a shader"), and your Copperleaf hitches were blamed on
    the ground setup, not compiles: H5 doesn't touch the ground setup.
  - The precompile list (walk-view-gl.js `ensureWalkGl`, not webgl.js) already had every new instanced and batched
    program, the shadows lane's two included.
- Changed (one kind per commit; files of other lanes: create and delete lines only):
  - The known bugs: engine/light.js `frameBlockLost()` and walk/sprites.js `hideQueriesLost()`, run on every restore.
  - The registry (engine/webgl.js, "resources"): `gpuBuffer/gpuTexture/gpuVao/gpuFramebuffer/gpuMake(type, kind,
    bytes)`, `gpuSized`, `gpuFree` (a handle of an older context is only forgotten; one made outside it is deleted by
    its type), `gpuRetire` (freed two frame ticks later), `gpuOnRestore(name, fn)`, `gpuMemory()`. Entries sit in a
    WeakMap and never keep an object alive; one collected without `gpuFree` counts as "dropped" (a leak's sign).
    `gpuState.gen` goes up with every context and restore; caches compare it. The frame scheduler's tick calls
    `gpuFrame()`: retired objects freed, and a context that died before its lost event is marked lost at once.
  - Moved onto it: the engine's own objects (quad, stand-ins, samplers, pictures, canvases, normal maps, render
    targets, meshes, GPU timers); programs and shaders (shaders deleted once linked; duplicates and failures
    deleted); buffers and vertex arrays in prop-models.js (both halves: I moved the shadow maps' record buffer's
    create line, `MODEL_SHADOW_INSTANCES`), model-instances.js, sprite-instances.js, buildings.js, structures.js,
    solid-props.js, walk/effects.js (rain), walk/grass-build.js, engine/light.js, walk/sprites.js (queries); the
    ground (ground-textures.js, map-cache.js, ground-mesh.js, water-data.js: kinds ground and ring); the world map
    (world-bowl.js). Left on purpose: self-test.js's probes (they delete their own).
  - Restore: the walk view's drop (`walkViewGpuLost`) and the world map's (`worldBowlDropGpu`) registered with
    `gpuOnRestore`; the registry runs every drop first, then the walk view and the map are handed back.
  - H3, debug log: `gpuMemory` in the report (MB, objects and dropped objects by kind, the picture cap's own count,
    pictures trimmed, contexts made, `lateCompiles`: the names behind `pcl`), `gmb` (total MB) in every sample.
  - H5: `quality.warmUp` ("Warm up before showing", on): a place fades in once two frames have drawn behind its fade
    (at most 1.5 s), `mountWalkView`'s promise waits for it; a restore fades out and back in the same way.
  - Debug menu: the diagnostics test's note says 4-5 min on a phone (the R1 measure lane's note for this lane).
- Verified: lint, typecheck, `npm test` (1132), check:modules after every commit; the smoke check on every commit
  touching game/ (run from a worktree of the commit). New tests: tools/test/gpu-registry.test.mjs (counts, sizes,
  free, retire, generations, the early loss, owners' drops, render targets, meshes, programs). One headless crash check

### Player visibility - you stay visible behind buildings and trees - 2026-10-25
Branch `ccr-bdf253b3-4vm5w6` (the session's own: the owner chose to work here instead of `fix/player-visibility`,
which didn't exist; one session's work, one PR). Not a phase: the owner asked for a system and approved the plan in
Plan Mode with these answers: all three layers (silhouette, see-through circle, a better whole-object fade); the
silhouette an outline in the colour of your top (lifted if dark); you and the one you talk to; the setting renamed
"Your outline when hidden". No tag (not a phase).
- What was there (TR-3, checked in the code): the silhouette and the rock's see-through circle only while ground cuts
  the camera's line (`rockK`); behind a house or tree on flat ground neither showed. A 0.4 fade written out twice
  (walk/sprites.js, solid-props.js): one test point, instant, props over 1.6 m, and **never the low-poly models**,
  which are Copperleaf's buildings (lab, shop, cottages: `M.model` with a door, not `M.build`).
- Changed (one cause per commit):
  - **logic/occlude.js** (new, tests occlude.test.mjs): `pictureCovers` (the cover test, moved first with no change),
    `hiddenEase`, `outlineColour`, `coverTarget`, `fadeEase`.
  - **Silhouette for anything that hides you** (sprites.js `drawPlayerSilhouette`): no `rockK` gate; an invisible first
    draw is an occlusion query (`ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED_CONSERVATIVE`), its answer `walkRenderer.hidT`, eased into `hidK`;
    pull toward the eye 0.8 m (was 0.6). Debug log: the camera line's `hidden`.
  - **Outline** (sprite shader `uGhostE`): the picture's edge whole, the inside dotted (`outlineFill`), in the top's
    colour (`lookOf`, the worn top's first colour, else the wardrobe's; looked up once a second). Engine > Camera
    `outline` (1 art pixel; 0 = the old dark blue tint), `outlineFill` (0.25).
  - **Talk partner**: while `talkBox.on`, the person or townsperson within 1.5 m of `walkRenderer.talkAt` gets the same
    outline in their own top's colour; not counted toward your `hidK`.
  - **See-through circle when hidden** (draw-common.js `rockUniformsFor`): on with `hidK` as well as `rockK`; the
    buildings' three shaders got ROCK_GLSL (the models, built on them, no longer add it). Engine > Camera `hideFade`,
    `hideSize` (0.3), `hideAmount` (0.7, capped at 0.85).
  - **Circle dither moved by (2, 1)** (walk-shaders.js `rockHides`): with the fades' own pattern, a picture both faded
    and in the circle lost every pixel, the query saw nothing and the circle flickered off (found in the pictures:
    lab, shop, a tree). Now at least 2 cells in 16 stay for any fade from 0.1 and circle up to 0.85.
  - **Whole-object fade** (walk/quality-cull.js `coverItems`, after culling): your feet, middle and head; to
    `coverFade` (0.4), halfway back while the circle is on; eased per placement (out about 0.25 s, back about 0.5 s);
    models and voxel props fade now (they read `it.fade`).

  - **Checks**: fast check "Behind things" (Copperleaf: hidden behind at least half of three buildings and three trees,
    four samples in a row, circle on; not in the open); "Tall ground" no longer expects no silhouette on flat ground (the
    mountains landing's bushes really cover you there; it checks no rise and no rock fade); tall-ground-draw tests for
    the query, the talk partner and the circle; `tools/look-behind.py` (pictures, validation/behind/, ignored).
- Where the plan was wrong: an occlusion query that says "how much" needs `SAMPLES_PASSED`, which WebGL2 doesn't have;
  `ANY_SAMPLES` is yes or no, so the "minimum amount hidden" filter is the 0.8 m pull alone (a lamp post in front of
  you turns the circle on; it only cuts what is in front of you inside it). No `?fixture=behind`: the spots are found

over matching layer names.

  `house_cottage`, …) is a low-poly model (`prop-models.js`), not a `buildings.js` building (`build` key: 18 legacy
  props, none placed by mapgen). The model's window is a plain blue box the low-poly shader never lit, and the only
  light was the old picture path's round glow (`walk/effects.js`, `e.k === 'window'`): a 0.32 m camera-facing disc at
  the picture's window spot, shifted along the camera's right (not the model's front) for an unturned prop, bloomed
  into a ball. A first plan aimed at `buildings.js` would have changed nothing the player sees.

  - Data: `tools/mark-window-glass.py` (one-off) gave the glass layers of the 19 models with picture windows a
    `glass` number (1-31; an arched top shares its window's). 126 layers; the lamp glass, solar panels and the
    clinic's roof dome are left out.
  - Engine: `lowPolyFromRecipe` writes the window into the vertex's spare byte 18 (0 ramp, 1 flat colour as the
    prebuilt meshes use it, 2-32 glass) and returns each window's middle and outward look (`wins`); `tagPropModel`
    sets `it.wins`. The model shader's `glassLit` (GLASS_GLSL): sky and a sun glint by day, a room's lamp after dark
    (warm, kitchen-cool or a TV's blue by a seed), soft roll-off so bloom spreads the window's own shape.
    `walk/lighting.js modelWindowLight`: each window's place, lit or not by `environmentWindowLit` at its own spot,
    strength 1 after dark, `lights.windowsDay` by day, 0 seen from inside a room; it also feeds the light on the
    ground (from the lit ground-floor glass, pushed out its own way). `effects.js` draws no window disc for an item
    with glass. With Props as low-poly off (voxels) nothing changes: no `wins`, the old disc.
  - Studio: the model editor's "Window glass" number on a shape layer.
  - `tools/look-windows.py`: Copperleaf pictures in front of a model building at noon, dusk, night, straight and
    turned (validation/look-windows/).
- Risky: the art cache is per version; a phone with the old model JSON cached has no glass numbers, so it keeps the old
  look (the disc) until the art cache refreshes. Glow strength (`e*1.6` against bloom threshold 0.9) was judged in
  software drawing only: check it on a phone at night.
- Verified: lint, typecheck, check:modules, prettier; `npm test` 919/919 (two new low-poly tests); check:data;
  `check:smoke` 6/6 (the Shaders step compiles the new model shader). `tools/look-windows.py` before (base 2cfef57)

### Phone speed, calmer effects, five times of day - 2026-10-23
Branch `claude/new-session-yby9e8` (one session, restarted from main after PR #170 merged). From the owner's three
debug logs of 2026-10-23 (Android phone, iPad, Windows) and their ask: the phone runs badly, menus are sluggish, blur
and haze toned down ("don't drop the blur, make it more subtle"), a stylized time of day with about five times to tune
in the Studio, and more suggestions (tech and visual).
- What the logs say (checked in the code):
  - Android in Copperleaf: **1,770 draw calls and 27,400 uniform calls a frame** (iPad 1,050 / 10,000); **864 sprite
    draws against the iPad's 191**: a phone held upright keeps about 1,000 of 1,530 things in view (the iPad 230).
  - On Android Chrome a wait on the graphics process shows up as main-thread time, so the automatic quality judged every
    slow frame "main-thread bound", held the effects at step 2 and pushed the resolution back to 1 every second: the
    phone ran the whole session at full resolution, 17-27 fps.
  - Phase 20 says the Android phone is limited by pixels: with engine.json's quality.resolution 1.5 it draws the 1.6 MP
    cap, but the calls are now the bigger cost. Stage E (instanced sprites) is the real fix.
  - Menus on a phone (portrait, under 960 px): a CSS blur on the full-screen live 3D canvas, glass blurs of 10-18 px on
    top, all redone every frame because the world kept drawing at 24 fps behind full screens.
- Changed (one cause per commit):
  - Menus: the blur behind a phone's screens 1.5 px to 0.8 px (kept, at the owner's word); the world behind a full
    screen settles for 0.8 s, then draws once a second (a still canvas keeps its blurred backdrop); phone glass blurs
    halved through CSS variables (a no-op commit first: the fixed values became variables with today's values);
    Billie pictures redraw at most 20 times a second (their pose moves in 50 ms steps).
  - Walk: the automatic quality's step is a pure function (logic/quality-step.js, tests); on Android and iPhone a slow
    frame now takes steps 3-4 and then the resolution (not below 0.6), never raising it for "main-thread" time.
    New settings Quality > Skip tiny props (minPropPx, 3 in the data) and Small props' distance on phones
    (phonePropDistance, 48 m in the data; small props under 1 m fade out over the last 8 m; buildings never). The
    effects pass skips props outside the view, and fountains outside it draw no spray.
  - Engine data, calmer: depth-of-field blur 2 to 1, behind you 2.6 to 1.4, sharp band 0.62 to 0.8, colour fringes 1.15
    to 0.35, vignette 0.72 to 0.4, bloom 0.8 to 0.6, glare 0.9 to 0.6, saturation 1.2 to 1.1, mist 0.16 to 0.08.
  - **Five times of day** (logic/time-of-day.js, tests): engine groups todDawn, todDay, todGolden, todDusk, todNight
    (25 dials each: hour offset and blend, sky colours and amount, light colour and strength, fill and its colour,
    haze colour, amount and distance, mist, exposure, saturation, contrast, warmth, shadow strength, shadow and
    highlight tints, glow, lamps, stars). Dawn sits at sunrise, day 3 h after it, golden hour 1.4 h before sunset, dusk
    0.4 h after, night 1.8 h after (all move with the season); each look is reached over its blend hours, the one before
    holds until then. They replace, outdoors, the old dawn/dusk/night sky tints, warm sun and moon colour, night ambient,
    saturation, exposure, warmth and bloom terms, the dawn mist and the lamps; weather, a scene's own look and the
    player's dials stay on top; rooms keep their light. The colours are game data (engine.json); the code's defaults

### Fix - the hub's "black screen" in the full quick check - 2026-10-23
Branch `fix/hub-frame-wait` (one session, docs/BRANCHES.md). The failure in RL-R1's long checks (PR #161's comment):
"Ground tiles, building plans and colours, rooms": `w:copperleaf* isn't drawing (black screen)`, under CPU load.
- Cause: the check, not the game. `go_scene` wanted 2 new frames within 30 s of a place opening. Once a minute the
  debug log takes its picture of the scene (`screenSnapshot`, `readPixels`), which makes the page wait for the software
  drawing to finish. That frame took 1.2-1.5 s on a fresh page (with or without 8-16 busy loops), but 16-23 s late in a
  14-minute desktop run (4 busy cores, or the unit tests looping beside it). One more slow frame in the same 30 s and
  the step failed. The screen was never black: the draw loop kept running (`frameScheduler.tasks.has('dio')`). On a
  phone's graphics chip that wait is a few milliseconds.
- Changed (tools/check-quick.py `go_scene` only; no game code, data or names): after 30 s without 2 frames, if the draw
  loop is still running it waits up to 60 s more and adds a note naming the slowest frame meanwhile. It fails only when
  the loop is gone ("stopped drawing: its draw loop is gone (black screen)") or fewer than 2 frames came in 90 s.
- Verified: a scratch probe on the hub, the old and the new `go_scene`. No new frame for 35 s: old fails with the
  PR #161 message, new passes with a note. The draw loop stopped (`frameStop('dio')`): both fail, the new one says so.
  "Ground tiles" and "Place views" pass with the unit tests looping beside them; the 12 desktop steps up to the hub
  step pass under load (the buddy lag in "Double and Alpha battles" is the known one, RF-2's entry). lint, typecheck,
  `npm test` (827), smoke (6 of 6). I could not get the natural failure itself on this machine: the stall reached
  20-23 s, short of 30.
- Risky: a step that goes through `go_scene` while frames are this slow now takes up to 60 s longer instead of failing.
- Found, not changed: tools/requirements-check.txt pins Playwright 1.56, which can't launch this machine's Chromium
  (1.63 works). And the frame scheduler (frame-scheduler.js `runFrameTasks`) drops a task for good when it throws, so
  one error in a walk frame would freeze the scene until it is mounted again. No sign of that here; worth its own look.
- Before merging: merge main again once RF-4 has merged, and run the checks again.

### Tooling - Repo admin workflow (tags and branch deletion for cloud sessions) - 2026-10-23
Branch `claude/optimistic-maxwell-vhge6s`. Not a phase: asked for by the owner so sessions can make tags and clean up
branches (the git proxy refuses both with HTTP 403).
- Changed: `.github/workflows/repo-admin.yml`, run by hand (workflow_dispatch). `create-tag`: a lightweight tag on a
  commit, names `legacy` or `<name>-done` only, an existing tag is never moved; on a `phase-*` tag it starts the Check
  workflow on the tag with `baseline=true`, since a tag made with GitHub's own token starts no workflows (a dispatched
  Check also runs the selftest job, which a pushed tag doesn't). `delete-branches`: never main, legacy, the default
  branch, archive/* or a branch with an open pull request; the run summary lists each branch's last commit.
  `dry_run` is on by default. docs/BRANCHES.md says to use it.
- Branch naming (owner's ask): docs/BRANCHES.md "Naming and long plans" (the kinds of branch and their names; a
  plan of several sessions lives on one `track/<plan>` branch named in its plan file, every session starts on it and
  checks it, the branch stays after its PRs merge) and a CLAUDE.md line pointing there. The workflow never deletes
  `track/*`. The old tip to turn on "Automatically delete head branches" is reversed: it would delete a track branch
  on every merge. Existing long branches (`sound`, `RL-10b`, ...) keep their names until their plans end.
- Risky: the workflow can delete branches and runs with `contents: write`. Anyone who can push could edit it on a
  branch and run that copy; only people with write access can run workflows at all. To limit it to main's copy, give
  the job a GitHub environment that only allows main (Settings -> Environments).
- Verified: actionlint clean; both scripts run against a stand-in `gh` (protected names, open PRs, missing branches,
  dry run, empty list, bad and existing tag names, the phase-tag Check start). Not run on GitHub yet: it must be on
  main first.
- Done after the merge (PR #146): dry runs of both actions on GitHub, then the `legacy` tag (0314a22) and the
  clean-up, 157 branches down to 22 (docs/BRANCHES.md lists what is left and why; each deleted branch's commit is in
  the Repo admin run summaries). Found: "Automatically delete head branches" is on (the owner should turn it off, see
  BRANCHES.md); `sound` holds SND-6, 13 commits, not merged and with no PR.

after Phase 2's worker (T2.4). The session stopped once on the usage limit and went on from the same branch.

### Phase 13 (part) - The fast check and the in-game graphics test - 2026-10-18
Two parts, plans approved by the owner. Part 1 on branch ccr-5f324dee-5mgqdn (merged as PR #16), Part 2 on top of it.
- Changed:
  - Part 1: `tools/check-fast.py` (`npm run check:fast`), the fast check, only what must never break: the data, the
    world-map graph, a town, a route, a cave and a room open and draw, a save round-trips, a battle plays to the end,
    the game boots with no errors, the Studio loads, and the exported debug log holds no names. `game/js/fixture.js`:
    `?fixture=<name>` (title, town, route, cave, room, battle, stored) starts a ready-made game with its own save key,
    never signed in, with the planted names in FIXTURE_NAMES (trainer "Quillonda", nickname "Zorblax"). The CI push
    job runs check-fast.py instead of the smoke set.
  - Part 2: `game/js/graphics-test.js`, the in-game graphics test. A button in Settings → Help ("Run the graphics
    test", `data-a="gfxtest"`) and one in the debug menu's Performance row. settings-screen.js (`startGraphicsTest`)
    loads it on demand (`import()` of `js/graphics-test.js` against the page's address, so the build leaves it as its
    own file in dist/game/js/) and hands it what it reads, so the module has no imports. Steps, all in Marigold Town:
    the shaders (the same check as check-quick.py's Shaders step, which is unchanged), the game defaults to compare
    with, each of the 144 ENGINE_SPEC dials on its own (through the player's expert dials, which come before a scene's
    look; a number at the top of its range or the bottom if that is its default, on/off flipped, a choice at another
    option, a colour at #FF4080, the light dials at night), Balanced and Beautiful, and the five ENGINE_PRESETS. Each
    step opens the scene from scratch and counts frames for 2 s: frame rate, longest frame, time to open, errors. An
    OK/Problem table and "Save the report" (a .json file: steps, numbers, errors, the graphics chip, screen and cores;
    not the browser, language or time zone). The last row is the planted-name check: the planted names, the trainer's
    name and every nickname in the save; any found is taken out and the row is a Problem.
  - Saving paused and the save put back as in self-test.js; the save copy also brings back the player's graphics
    settings (aim, expert dials), and the scene is made again with them, when the test ends, is stopped or fails.
    selfTest.on is set while it runs, so the story, postcards and the full test stay out of the way.
  - `tools/test/graphics-test.test.mjs` (6 tests): every dial gets a step at a value other than its default, the
    names list, a clean report passes, a planted name is taken out and fails the check, the report's fields.
  - eslint.config.js: a block for graphics-test.js (it is on no page). to-module put ENGINE_*, FIXTURE_NAMES, the
    shader sets, gpuState, compileProgram and attributeClashes through hooks.js for settings-screen.js.
  - Docs: TESTING.md (the graphics test and its rules), CHANGELOG.
- Risky or unfinished:
  - **The graphics test has never run.** As the owner asked, Claude ran it in no browser at all, not even software
    rendering. It must be run on a real device; the first run is the owner's. The likeliest trouble: a scene that
    takes long to open from scratch on a phone (the step limit is 30 s), and the whole run's length (153 steps, about
    3-4 s each: probably 8-10 minutes, not measured).
  - The spec's "Saver" preset doesn't exist: the Graphics tab has Balanced and Beautiful only (Battery saver was
    removed in phase 03). Both are tested; Beautiful is the same look as the game defaults row.
  - Dials a scene doesn't use (water with no water in view, lamp shadows by day) show OK without showing much.
  - The steps read the frame count of the walk view only; the battle stage and the world map aren't in it.
- Verified (what ran, what passed): `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (31 tests), `npm run
  check:modules`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:data`, `npm run build` (graphics-test.js in dist/game/js,
  the bundle keeps the import as written), and `python3 tools/check-fast.py`: 11 of 11 passed in 112 s on 2 browsers
  in this container. A planted fault (the name check turned off) fails its unit test; a planted undefined name in
  graphics-test.js fails lint. Part 1, from its session: check-fast takes about 85 s on 2 browsers (1 browser 94.5 s,
  4 browsers 110.8 s), and all 11 planted faults were caught.
- Decisions I made (and why): the dials go through the player's expert dials, because a scene's own look comes
  before the game-wide defaults and would hide some dials. Each dial moves away from its default, so every step
  changes something. Each step opens the scene from scratch, so dials read while a scene is made count. Device
  details are cut to the graphics chip and the screen, because the user agent, language and time zone say more
  about the player than a graphics report needs.
- Questions waiting for the owner: the first run on a phone, and the report it saves.
- Next session starts with: the report from that run; then the rest of phase 13 (13b, 13c).

### Phase 04d - Modernize: the window bridge removed - 2026-10-18
Owner's choices: generated hooks instead of forward imports (after the first plan failed, see Decisions); opt-in test
globals; JSDoc + .d.ts for TypeScript; this session is the bridge only, TypeScript and boundaries are 04e, which ends
with `phase-04-done`.
- Changed:
  - Nothing in the game or the Studio reaches a module's names as globals any more. A module imports from EARLIER
    modules directly; what it reads from a LATER module (154 names), or from whichever module the page has (the
    renderer shared with the Studio reading S, GD, RM, MOVES, sfx...; 64), it imports from game/js/hooks.js, a slot
    per name that the declaring module fills with provide(): functions at the top, other values right after their
    declaration (the timing the bridge had). 212 names in all. Page order and script tags are unchanged.
  - Setters for everything one module changes in another (an imported name can't be assigned): core.js setS, setB,
    setRM, setSaveHold, setNoSaving (the test mode); diorama.js and map.js for the 3D versions diorama-gl.js and
    map-gl.js put in place; battle.js and talk.js for extras.js's wraps; core.js setSave and map-gl.js setMglRender
    for the in-game full test; the Studio's swaps (engine source, dglAdapt, dioMount, rigParts, dioData, dioImg,
    artLoad, api, saveAll, toast, render, getP/setP, pedDraw). Each setter also updates hooks.js. Nothing renamed.
  - The Studio's inline shim script (S, U, B, RM, esc, the live data tables) is a module, studio/js/shims.js.
  - The debug log: log.js (classic, runs first) reads GAME.x instead of 25 module names, and NWLOG.hook wraps through
    GAME[name] instead of window[name]. game/js/log-names.js (generated, the last module of the game's page) fills
    GAME with getters and with setters for the ~45 functions the log wraps or times; the tool writes a setter into
    a module's generated part where it has none.
  - game/js/bridge.js is game/js/test-globals.js and puts the modules' names on window only with
    window.PB_TEST_GLOBALS = true (check-quick, check-game, check-studio-github and the art builders set it with an
    init script; their page.evaluate calls are unchanged) or ?globals in the address (the phone console).

    checks the load order (nothing a module reads while it loads, directly or through what it calls then, may come
    from a module that hasn't run). It caught a real case: boot.js calls accInit() at load, which reads NW_TEST.
  - ESLint lints every script with only the classic scripts' names as globals: a module name used without an import
    (or by a classic script) is a no-undef error. Planted toast() in tapdebug.js: caught.

### Phase 04c - Modernize: ES modules - 2026-10-17
Owner's choices: conversion tool applied backwards from boot.js in batches; keep a window bridge through 04c; no
minifying.
- Changed:
  - Every game and Studio script is an ES module (74, plus game/js/bridge.js), except the classic ones on purpose:
    version.js (sw.js importScripts it), the art manifests and gamedata.js (generated data), data-files.js (the Node
    tools run it too), data-fallback.js (the synchronous data read), log.js and tapdebug.js (they catch errors before
    the modules run, and still work if a module fails to load on a phone).
  - tools/to-module.mjs (`npm run modules`; `npm run check:modules` in CI) writes the top of each module between the
    to-module markers: imports of what it reads from EARLIER modules of its page(s), `export` on what others import,
    and expose({...}). It imports a name only if every page loading the file loads the same module earlier, and the
    file never assigns it. Imports only point back, so modules run in the page's order, as the scripts did.
  - The window bridge (game/js/bridge.js): every module's top-level names are on window as a getter and a setter of
    the module's own variable. That is how a module reaches a LATER file's names (the cycles), names it assigns (S, B,
    RM, SAVE_HOLD, map-gl.js replacing map.js's functions, diorama-gl.js replacing dioNav/dioStop/dioProj/dioUnproject,
    extras.js wrapping openBattle/endBattle/talkFolk, the Studio's swaps) and names each page defines its own way
    (S, U, B, RM, esc, the Studio's live tables, the battle HUD hooks). The debug log's and the diagnostics' wrappers
    (`window.render = wrapped`) change the module's own variable, so calls inside and between modules are still timed.
    198 game names and 107 Studio names are still reached this way (the bundle renames their module variable, e.g.
    `DIO$1`); everything else is imported (569 import lines).
  - `$`, `$$`, `rnd`, `clamp` moved to game/js/util.js, loaded first by both pages (they were in core.js and the
    Studio's inline stand-ins). Reached through the bridge, `clamp` couldn't be inlined into the ground height code:
    the loader took ~5 s (17%) longer on an emulated phone. Now on par.
  - `npm run build` bundles each page's modules into one file (dist/game/js/game-<hash>.js, 1.5 MB, 470 KB gzipped;
    dist/studio/js/studio-<hash>.js), not minified, with a source map; one file per page so the
    order is the page's. The module sources are left out of dist/. The dev server serves every script as on disk.
  - ESLint lints module scripts as modules and refuses a name a module shares with another script of its page (in a
    module, no-redeclare can't see that). check-quick's duplicate-function check reads module tags and `export`.
  - check-quick v35 no longer counts art/next/tiles (deleted in phase 03; it failed "tiles: 0 variants" on the base).
  - tools/check-studio-github.py: the Studio in GitHub mode against a local stand-in for the API (sign-in, the data
    files, every section, an edit proposed as a pull request). Not in CI yet.

### Phase 02 - Security - 2026-10-16
- Changed:
  - Firestore rules moved out of the README into firebase/firestore.rules (the only copy) with 13 emulator tests
    (firebase/test/rules.test.mjs; `cd firebase && npm ci && npm test`; CI job `rules` on every push). Friends are found
    by code only: users/ and codes/ can't be listed (the old `allow read` let any signed-in player download everyone's
    page and place), a page is readable by its owner and the friends on the owner's own list, only the receiver accepts
    a request (the old rules let a sender accept their own), writes are checked for shape and size.
  - friends.js: a friend's page that isn't shared back yet is retried every minute (no error); friend pages and request
    names are cleaned before drawing (frClean).
  - Names: cleanName() strips < > " & ` and control characters where names enter (nickname box, cleanLook, migrate), so
    the ~60 templates that put N(m) into HTML unescaped are safe. tools/check-data-text.py (CI) guards game data text.
  - saveVersion (core.js SAVE_VERSION = 1): saves without it are refused with "This save is from an older version of
    the game and can't be loaded in this one", a new game starts, the old save is kept aside in the browser
    (`<key>-set-aside`, `-cloud-set-aside`). A newer save is never written over (SAVE_HOLD). Backups from other versions
    are refused. Account saves carry saveVersion.
  - docs/SECURITY.md: the review (claims, rules, API key, App Check, Studio token options, innerHTML table, phase 18
    data design, one friends bug found).
- Risky or unfinished:
  - The new rules are NOT live until the owner publishes them (Firebase console). The game works with old and new rules.
  - Old account saves are replaced on the account once the player plays on in this version (a copy stays in that
    browser). That is a cloud-data wipe in slow motion: owner to confirm (question below).
  - phase-01-done and phase-02-done tags: this session can't push tags (the push is refused); the owner adds them.
  - Friends: making friends again "the other way round" after a removal fails (pre-existing, not security; SECURITY.md).
- Verified (what ran, what passed):
  - Rules tests: 13/13 on the new rules; 8 of 13 fail on the old README rules (the tests catch what was open).
  - Headless probes on the real page: cleanName/frClean/migrate strip markup and keep apostrophes; no save, an old save,
    a current save and a newer save each start, keep aside, load or hold as intended, with the message showing.
  - check-globals: 0 duplicates. check-data-text: clean. `--smoke`: 13/13 (114 s). Full check: not run for phase 02 (owner: run it once at the end of phase 03).
- Decisions I made (and why): rules live in firebase/ (testable, one copy) and the README points there; names are
  cleaned at the way in rather than escaping 60 templates now (phase 06 replaces the rendering); saveVersion is a save
  FORMAT number (1), not the game version: it should only change when old saves can't be read, which is rarer than
  releases (phase 03 reads it from the version file next to the game version); a newer save is held, never overwritten.
